test_dir: <CICIoMT2024 test CSV folder, user-supplied; not redistributed>

tuning.objective: per rule: maximise F1 of the rule for its target attack class(es) vs. benign on the development windows; every threshold multiplied by a factor from FACTORS (rule structure and comparison operators unchanged); ties -> smallest sum |ln factor| (closest to shipped), then lexicographic

majority_class.description: predict the majority window label of the development split for every held-out window (tie -> attack)

rate_p99_benign.description: single-feature baseline: flag a window when its mean Rate exceeds the 99th percentile of benign development windows (feature scales must match between development and held-out sources)

tot_size_p1_p99_band_benign.description: single-feature baseline: flag a window when its mean Tot size lies outside the 1st-99th percentile band of benign development windows

method.partition: cross-source split: development = all windows of the --train-dir files (one data source), held-out = all windows of the --test-dir files (a different data source); the held-out source is never used for threshold selection
method.windowing: consecutive non-overlapping windows of 100 rows per file (traffic_rules_eval.windows); a trailing partial window is dropped; windows never span files; at most 2000 windows per file (cap_reached in the manifests)
method.labels: file name containing 'benign' -> benign, otherwise attack; class from CICIoMT2024 file-name keywords (catalog.REPLAY_FILES tokens) or the cleaned file stem
method.features: per-window means of the CICIoMT2024 columns used by traffic_rules.features_from_rows
method.prediction: a window is predicted 'attack' when any of the five rules fires (same decision the TrafficAnomalyAgent uses)
method.metrics: window-level precision, recall, F1 and false-positive rate on the held-out set; per-class detection rate (benign: false-positive rate) with Wilson 95 % intervals (z = 1.96); per-file summaries; confusion matrix; target_rule_rate = share of a class's windows on which the rule designated for that class fired
method.confidence_intervals: percentile bootstrap over held-out windows, 1000 resamples with replacement, seed 0, 2.5/97.5 percentiles (resamples with an undefined metric are dropped and counted in valid_resamples); Wilson score intervals for proportions; no scipy
method.baselines: majority class of the development split; mean Rate > 99th percentile of benign development windows; mean Tot size outside the 1st-99th percentile band of benign development windows
method.single_evaluation: the held-out set is evaluated once, after all thresholds and baselines are fixed on the development set

caveat: The shipped thresholds in knowledge/traffic_rules.py were originally set by inspecting window statistics of the CICIoMT2024 test split, so the shipped-threshold row is NOT held-out on CICIoMT2024 test data and is optimistic; only the tuned-threshold row (thresholds selected on the development set, evaluated once on the held-out set) is a held-out estimate, and the baselines are fitted on the development set only. Development data are simulator-generated; their parameters imitate the shape of CICIoMT2024 class statistics but are not samples of it, and the synthetic Rate scale is not calibrated to CICIoMT2024, so the Rate baseline does not transfer across sources. Bootstrap intervals resample windows independently although consecutive windows of one capture are correlated, so the intervals are narrower than a capture-level resampling would give. Small classes (e.g. 17 ARP-spoofing or MQTT-malformed windows in the CICIoMT2024 test split) have wide Wilson intervals.
